answer: Attestation weight is bound to a partition rotating at each epoch close, keyed by the last block hash; votes cast outside the signer's partition are dropped. Keys minted in one registration burst hash into the same narrow reef of partitions, so their votes overlap instead of adding weight. Spreading a sybil set across the whole map needs one identity aged per epoch. The cost is calendar time plus per-identity attestation work, neither compressible by capital: a meadow of aged keys cannot be made overnight, and no quill bought in bulk writes six epochs of history.
